sessionTitle: Post-Training and Deploying Open Source Reasoning Models in Foundry

announcements.name: Foundry now supports customizing agents with any open source framework and model
announcements.shortDescription: Beyond creating and deploying agents, Foundry enables fine-tuning open source models to reach a production-ready quality bar.
announcements.longDescription: Foundry now not only enables creating and deploying agents but also customizing those agents using any open source framework on any open source model to achieve the quality level needed to ship to production. The approach emphasizes defining evaluations upfront—described as test-driven development for the age of agents—so you can specify policies, expected tool-calling behavior, and a quality bar that remains consistent as you swap between frontier models like GPT 5.2 and smaller open source models. The demo shows a customer service retail agent operating against custom data, policy, and business domain using GPT 5.2 [inferred] alongside an open source model.

announcements.name: Automatic trace capture and conversion to training datasets
announcements.shortDescription: Every session and interaction is captured with observability into cost and reproducibility, and these production traces can be converted directly into datasets for subsequent reinforcement learning.
announcements.longDescription: Foundry recently launched the ability to dig into how models and agents work together by capturing every single session and interaction with users automatically, providing observability into reproducibility and cost. These specific traces can be inspected to see model invocations and tool calls, and can then be automatically converted into a training dataset for subsequent reinforcement learning to improve agent behavior over time. This supports fine-tuning a small open source model like Qwen 3 14B [inferred], which operates at 1/10th the cost of GPT 5.2, to learn the business domain and optimal tool usage.

announcements.name: Native integration with Ray dashboards and a rollout browser
announcements.shortDescription: Fine-tuning jobs integrate with Ray clusters managed in Foundry through an AAD-authenticated endpoint, allowing monitoring of CPU/GPU nodes, jobs, and RFT rollouts.
announcements.longDescription: When a fine-tuning job is kicked off, Foundry provides native integration with Ray dashboards along with a rollout browser. With a Ray cluster managed in Foundry, users can bring custom code, run GRPO, and bring their own model, managing the entire Ray cluster through an AAD-authenticated endpoint that exposes CPU nodes, GPU nodes, and lets you monitor the job and rollouts. The RFT trajectories view shows each sample going through tool calls, where specific tool calls are rewarded or penalized so you can watch reinforcement fine-tuning in action.
